images.caption: Figure 2:Action tails recover a 10-step Gaussian prediction in fewer steps.Tail initialization crosses the Gaussian baseline in four steps forπ0.5\pi_{0.5}and six for SmolVLA on both benchmarks. Subtle shaded bands mark these earliest shared operating points.

Figure 3:Action tails require sample-dependent refinement.Each bar shows the fraction of samples with a given optimal denoising stepN∗N^{*}. Green denotesN∗N^{*}at or below the model-specific median (8 forπ0.5\pi_{0.5}, 9 for SmolVLA), while red denotesN∗N^{*}above it. Dashed lines mark the median boundaries; brackets report the fraction of samples in each region. Means and standard deviations appear inside the panels.

Figure 4:Overview of VLA-Rolling.VLA-Rolling reuses the unexecuted action tail from the previous inference round by estimating its confidence, which jointly determines tail preservation and the adaptive denoising budget while keeping the original VLA frozen.(a) VLA-Rolling inference.The Action Confidence Estimator predicts a confidence which controls its interpolation with Gaussian noise. The resulting initialization is refined usingNadaptN_{\mathrm{adapt}}denoising steps. The executable prefix is sent to the robot, while the remaining tail rolls into the next round.(b) VLA-Rolling training.Confidence labels are constructed from the quality of inherited actions and normalized with EMA-based quantile statistics.
